messages.content: Crisis Resolved. Mediterranean Security Forum concluding session. SGDSN requires recommendations for the Toulon Declaration on Regional Maritime Cybersecurity.

questions.question: [QUIZ] EU/NATO + POLITICAL CELL — REGIONAL ARCHITECTURE (D-04)

options.label: A → Establish EU CERT Med (dedicated Mediterranean maritime cyber cell)
B → Issue non-binding voluntary best-practice guidelines for port operators
C → Delegate incident coordination entirely to national CERTs
D → Mandate binding IMO cyber certification for entry to Med ports

questions.note: Combining EU CERT Med (A) and binding IMO certification (D) establishes a complete regional and legal deterrent framework.

questions.question: [QUIZ] DIPLOMATIC CORE — MARITIME LAW REFORM

options.label: A → UNCLOS (UN Convention on the Law of the Sea)
B → SOLAS (Safety of Life at Sea)
C → Budapest Convention on Cybercrime
D → Chicago Convention on Civil Aviation

questions.note: UNCLOS was drafted before the cyber era and does not define cyber operations as 'non-innocent passage' or sabotage.

questions.question: [QUIZ] PORT POLICY — NIS2 COMPLIANCE GAPS

options.label: A → Small feeder ports and vessels operating under flags of convenience
B → Major container terminals and LNG import docks
C → State-owned naval shipyards and military harbors
D → Trans-national shipping alliance headquarters

questions.note: Flags of convenience allow vessels to operate with minimal cyber oversight, creating weak entry points into major ports.

questions.question: [QUIZ] REGIONAL GOVERNANCE — TRANS-MEDITERRANEAN TRUST

options.label: A → Create a joint Maritime Cyber Hub under neutral third-party facilitation (e.g. IMO or NATO Hub)
B → Require full integration into EU command networks as a condition for trade
C → Limit cooperation to commercial technology export licenses only
D → Avoid cooperation due to persistent geopolitical trust deficits

questions.note: A neutral regional hub allows shared threat monitoring and capacity building without compromising internal EU infrastructure.

questions.question: [VOTE] STRATEGIC VOTE — CYBER RESILIENCE FUNDING

options.label: A → Direct EU / NATO defense budget reallocation
options.note: Secures strategic funding but subject to political approval delays

options.label: B → Public-private cost-sharing with commercial terminal operators
options.note: Balances responsibility but risks fragmented implementation

options.label: C → Mandate a 'cyber security levy' on all commercial cargo tonnage
options.note: Reliable funds but fiercely opposed by shipping lobbies

options.label: D → Rely on volunteer contributions from member states
options.note: Highly unstable, fails to secure critical operations

questions.note: Reallocating regional defense budgets establishes cybersecurity as a core sovereignty capability.

questions.question: [VOTE] STRATEGIC VOTE — GEOPOLITICAL RESPONSE ALIGNMENT

options.label: A → Wait for unanimous EU/NATO intelligence consensus
options.note: High legitimacy, protects alliance cohesion but slows response

options.label: B → Unilateral actions: immediate diplomatic and financial countermeasures to show resolve
options.note: Deterrence signal but risks major trade fallout if wrong

options.label: C → Pursue unilateral sanctions immediately without ally coordination
options.note: Isolates France and weakens collective security posture

options.label: D → Refer the case to the International Court of Justice
options.note: Takes years, completely useless for active crisis containment

questions.note: Waiting for unanimous EU/NATO consensus ensures high international legitimacy and sanction alignment.

questions.question: [VOTE] STRATEGIC VOTE — IMO STANDARD ENFORCEMENT

options.label: A → Port State Control: Detention of non-compliant vessels in regional harbors
options.note: Strongest enforcement but causes logistics delay risk

options.label: B → Financial penalties: Higher port entry fees for non-certified ships
options.note: Creates revenue but allows wealthy operators to bypass safety

options.label: C → Voluntary certification with insurance premium discount incentives
options.note: Low friction but slow and incomplete adoption rate

options.label: D → Self-declaration by vessel masters without physical audits
options.note: Useless paper exercise, easily bypassed by adversaries

questions.note: Enforcing the standard via Port State Control detention yields the highest and fastest compliance rates.

questions.question: [OPEN] OPEN SITREP — UNCLOS REFORM ADVOCACY
questions.prompt: Draft a policy proposal defining cyber-attacks on maritime assets as 'non-innocent passage' under UNCLOS.

questions.question: [OPEN] OPEN SITREP — REGIONAL HUB COOPERATION
questions.prompt: Propose the governance and voting structure for the new Mediterranean Maritime CERT.

questions.question: [OPEN] OPEN SITREP — MEDITERRANEAN FORUM DELIVERABLE
questions.prompt: Identify the single most critical policy recommendation your team will present to the Mediterranean Forum concluding session.
